name: Agreement Gauge
description: A laboratory alignment gauge for the DOT PRODUCT. Two grabbable arrows rise from the origin — a (warm amber) and b (cooler orange). A floating slab shows a self-substituting three-line equation: a.b = ax*bx + ay*by + az*bz, the same with the numbers plugged in, and the result; stacked beneath it the geometric form a.b = |a||b|cos(theta) lands on the SAME number. The live angle theta reads at the arc midpoint. A red->grey->green rail with a sliding puck tracks cos(theta) so the sign of the dot product is readable without a digit: green = agreeing, grey notch = perpendicular (a.b = 0, strangers), red = opposing. A |b| dial scales b without turning it; a SNAP 90 button parks b perpendicular to a. The result is computed, never grabbed.
theoreticalGrounding: The dot product does not measure length — it measures how much two directions agree. a.b = |a||b|cos(theta): at 0 degrees the product peaks at |a||b| (full agreement), at 90 degrees it is zero (pure perpendicularity, strangers), past 90 it goes negative (opposition). The algebraic component sum and the geometric magnitude*cosine form are visibly the same scalar.
